gaps.what: Who held Nellore 1263-1281: no land is drawn. Ganapati_Deva has the brothers of Manuma-siddhi II ruling Nellore 'as Pandya vassals' (no year); Rudrama_Devi has Naga-deva a Kakatiya vassal 1271-1275 and the Telugu Choda Tiru-kalatti-deva II at Nellore c. 1279-1283 (it also says he displaced Naga-deva 'in 1263'); Ambadeva has Vijaya Ganda-gopala holding Nellore until 1279 (implied).

Date of Manuma Ganda-gopala's restoration stays a bridge (1281): Rudrama_Devi 'sometime before 1281', Ambadeva 'sometime before 1282', while his 1284 Kodavaluru inscription is dated to his third regnal year.

Tikka's extension 'as far south as the river Kaveri' (1223-1248) is undated and names no place; the four districts stay circles because the gazetteer lacks Kadapa, Chittoor, Chengalpattu and Tondaimandalam.
Year of the Kakatiya installation of Tikka (vassal_start 1208, confidence 1) is a bridge from 'ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208'; the page gives no year.

Year of the Kollam (Desinganadu) branch's separation stays 1317 at confidence 1: the Venad page says only 'in the early 14th century CE, the Venadu rulers moved to Kallada, Kollam'; the Kollam page has no such branch and no date.

Chera vassalage 844-1005 is a bridge (844 is the Chera dossier's start; the Venad page's dated sign is c. 849, Ayyan Adikal under 'his overlord, the medieval Chera ruler'); the page also has Venad in a Chera inscription c. 1102, so the real vassalage probably lasted to 1124, but the dossier holds no land 1005-1123.
The c. 1275 Pandya capture of Kollam may be a vassalage (Ravi_Varma_Kulasekhara: 'ruled as a vassal'), not a loss; left as a loss because pandya-empire draws the land as its own until 1312.
